jararaca.moleculeNote: Teprotide (SQ 20,881) reproduces the venom peptide BPP-9a. Its first residue is L-pyroglutamate, not ordinary glutamate.
jararaca.mechanism: ACE inhibition reduces conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II and also slows bradykinin breakdown.
jararaca.bridge: Teprotide established that ACE inhibition could lower blood pressure. Medicinal chemistry produced an orally active, non-peptide inhibitor: captopril.
jararaca.drugNote: Captopril is synthesized. It is neither extracted venom nor the teprotide peptide.
jararaca.anatomy: Paired venom glands behind the eyes connect through ducts to hollow, hinged upper fangs.

timeline.label: Sérgio Ferreira reports bradykinin-potentiating activity in venom.
Ondetti, Rubin and Cushman report designed, orally active ACE inhibitors.
Captopril receives US approval for hypertension.

jararaca.structureNote: Illustrative computed conformer from the exact stereochemical graph of PubChem CID 443376. Not an experimentally determined fold and not a binding pose. Lowest MMFF94 energy among 12 generated conformers; seed 20881. N-terminal pyroglutamate is explicitly modeled. Target view: 1UZF is a crystal structure of human testicular ACE with captopril, not a teprotide–ACE complex.

gila.moleculeNote: Exendin-4 is a 39-residue peptide isolated from Gila monster venom. Exenatide is its synthetic drug counterpart.
gila.mechanism: GLP-1 receptor activation increases glucose-dependent insulin secretion, reduces inappropriately elevated glucagon and slows gastric emptying.
gila.mechanismShort: Activate GLP-1R. Support glucose-dependent insulin release.
gila.bridge: Isolation of exendin-4 led to synthetic exenatide, formulated for subcutaneous delivery.
gila.drugNote: Ozempic (semaglutide) is a modified human GLP-1 analogue, not an exendin-4 derivative.
gila.anatomy: Venom is made in glands of the lower jaw and reaches grooved lower teeth during a bite.

timeline.label: John Eng and colleagues report isolation of exendin-4.

gila.structureNote: First deposited NMR conformer, measured in 30% trifluoroethanol. The conformation is condition-dependent and is not a receptor-bound pose. The deposited 1JRJ model includes a terminal OXT atom; mature exendin-4/exenatide is C-terminally amidated. Treat this as an experimental backbone reference, not an atom-for-atom drug formulation.

sources.label: Semaglutide is a human GLP-1 analogue · FDA label

cone.moleculeNote: ω-conotoxin MVIIA is a disulfide-rich venom peptide. Ziconotide is its synthetic equivalent.
cone.mechanism: Blockade of N-type (CaV2.2) calcium channels in spinal pain pathways reduces neurotransmitter release.
cone.mechanismShort: Block calcium entry. Reduce pain-signal transmission.
cone.bridge: Chemical synthesis reproduces the peptide and its three disulfide bonds. Delivery into spinal fluid brings the drug to its site of action.
cone.drugNote: Prialt is administered by intrathecal infusion for severe chronic pain in selected patients. It is not an oral analgesic.
cone.anatomy: A venom duct connects to a proboscis that deploys a hollow, harpoon-like radular tooth.
cone.structureNote: First deposited NMR conformer. 25 amino acids; the terminal NH2 chemical group is not a 26th amino acid. Three disulfide bridges.

sources.label: Conus magus venom apparatus · original research

echis.modifications: Four disulfides; RGD motif at residues 24–26
echis.moleculeNote: Echistatin is a 49-residue disintegrin with an exposed RGD recognition motif.
echis.mechanism: Tirofiban prevents fibrinogen binding to platelet GP IIb/IIIa (αIIbβ3), inhibiting platelet aggregation.
echis.mechanismShort: Block fibrinogen bridges. Limit platelet aggregation.
echis.bridge: The integrin-binding motif of venom disintegrins informed small-molecule mimetics, including tirofiban.
echis.drugNote: Tirofiban is a synthesized non-peptide medicine, not isolated echistatin.
echis.anatomy: Venom glands supply hollow, hinged upper fangs through ducts.

timeline.label: Merck researchers report purified echistatin and its platelet-inhibitory activity.
Merck researchers report non-peptide fibrinogen-receptor antagonists.

echis.structureNote: First deposited NMR conformer; mature 49-residue echistatin. Four disulfide bridges; integrin-recognition RGD motif at positions 24–26. No expression-tag residues.

bee.modifications: Representative allergen Api m 1; not the entire medicine
bee.moleculeNote: Api m 1 (phospholipase A₂) is one important venom allergen. Apitoxin means bee venom, a mixture; it is not a single peptide.
bee.mechanism: Repeated, medically supervised venom-allergen exposure can reduce the severity of allergic reactions to future stings; multiple immune mechanisms contribute.
bee.mechanismShort: Build immune tolerance. Reduce reactions to future stings.
bee.bridge: A standardized venom extract is formulated for specialist-supervised allergy immunotherapy.
bee.drugNote: The clinical product contains a venom mixture. Showing one allergen does not mean that isolated Api m 1 is the marketed treatment.
bee.anatomy: Venom glands supply a reservoir linked to the stinger at the tip of a female worker’s abdomen.
bee.structureNote: Honeybee venom phospholipase A2 (Api m 1), 134 residues, shown as one representative allergen. Clinical venom immunotherapy uses a standardized mixture, not this isolated molecule. Bound analogue, calcium, waters and carbohydrate omitted.
